_comment: PII Processing and Transparency Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; r5-only privacy family with 8 base controls. PT is part of the NIST 800-53 r5 PRIVACY baseline rather than the LOW / MODERATE / HIGH security baselines — most users authoring this plan should select 'nist-privacy' in the baseline picker. Pairs with RA (RA-8 PIA is the entry point; categorization governs scope), AC (PT-2 / PT-3 authorize and limit processing — overlaps AC family), AT (PT-3 awareness training maps to AT-2 / AT-3), AU (PT-4 / PT-5 records overlap audit pipeline), and SI (SI-12(2) PII minimization echoes PT-3(2) data minimization).
family_name: Personally Identifiable Information Processing and Transparency
title: PII Processing and Transparency Plan
description: Documents how the system manages PII processing authority, lawful purpose, transparency to data subjects, consent, system-of-records notices, individual rights (access / amendment), and dissemination across third parties. Covers the controls of the PT family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. § 552a), E-Government Act of 2002 (Section 208 — PIA), OMB M-03-22 (PIA guidance), OMB M-17-12 (breach response), NIST IR 8062 (Privacy Risk Management Framework), NIST IR 8112 (Attribute Metadata), GDPR / state privacy laws where applicable, and Fair Information Practice Principles (FIPPs).
intro_template:
This PII Processing and Transparency Plan documents the privacy approach for {system_name}. It establishes the practices, criteria, cadences, and roles used to authorize and limit PII processing, communicate with data subjects through privacy notices, manage consent, publish System of Records Notices (SORNs) where applicable, support individual rights of access and amendment, and govern dissemination of PII to third parties.

The scope covers PT-1 through PT-8 within the {system_name} authorization boundary. Note: PT controls apply to systems that process PII; if {system_name} does not process PII, this plan documents that determination and the scope is reduced accordingly. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (PII Processing and Transparency family), NIST IR 8062 (Privacy Risk Management Framework), the Privacy Act of 1974, and OMB privacy guidance.
approach_template:
{system_name} PII processing is governed by {privacy_program_role} who maintains the privacy program documentation at {privacy_program_location}. The system's Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is at {pia_location}; System of Records Notices (where applicable) are at {sorn_location}. Individual privacy rights — access, amendment, and complaint — are administered through {individual_rights_workflow}. Third-party dissemination is governed by {third_party_governance_role} per the agreements register at {agreements_register_location}.

Additional details on processing authority, lawful purpose, consent, privacy notices, system-of-records notices, individual access, amendment / correction, and dissemination are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Privacy-program performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (PIA currency, SORN currency, privacy-notice currency, individual-rights-request response-time SLA compliance, consent-completion rate, third-party agreement currency, privacy-incident count). The PIA is reviewed on the cadence in §6.2; significant changes (new information collection, new processing purpose, new dissemination recipient) trigger immediate updates rather than waiting for the next periodic cycle. Privacy incidents are coordinated with the IR plan workflow under OMB M-17-12 breach-response timelines.
integration_template: This PII Processing and Transparency Plan does not stand alone. The RA family supplies RA-8 PIA as the entry-point activity (often co-authored with PT-2 authority documentation); the AC family enforces PT-2 / PT-3 processing limits at the access-control layer; the AT family delivers PT-3 awareness training; the AU family captures PT-4 / PT-5 records in the audit pipeline; the SI family's SI-12(1) PII limitation and SI-12(2) test-data minimization echo PT-3(2); the IR family handles privacy incidents per OMB M-17-12 breach-response. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where PT-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Roles and locations that anchor the rest of the plan.

questions.label: PII-in-scope determination
options: Yes — system processes PII (PT family fully applicable)
Yes — system processes a limited set of PII (some PT controls scoped)
No — system does not process PII (PT family non-applicable; documented determination per RA-8)

questions.label: Privacy-program role (one-liner)
questions.help: Role accountable for the privacy program (e.g., 'Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP)', 'Chief Privacy Officer', 'Privacy Officer + delegate to ISSO').

questions.label: Privacy-program documentation location
questions.help: Where privacy-program policy, procedures, and registers are maintained.

questions.label: PIA location (RA-8 cross-reference)
questions.help: Where the system's Privacy Impact Assessment lives. Per E-Government Act Section 208 + OMB M-03-22.

questions.label: SORN(s) location
questions.help: Where applicable System of Records Notices (SORNs) are published / cited. Per Privacy Act § (e)(4).

questions.label: Individual-rights workflow (one-liner)
questions.help: Brief phrase describing how individuals exercise rights of access / amendment / complaint (e.g., 'Privacy Act request portal at agency.gov/privacy', 'Mailbox privacy@agency.gov triaged by Privacy Office').

questions.label: Third-party-dissemination governance role
questions.help: Role accountable for third-party agreements involving PII (e.g., 'Privacy Officer with General Counsel concurrence').

questions.label: Third-party agreements register location
questions.help: Where MOUs / DSAs / Computer Matching Agreements / Routine Use authorizations are registered.

family_questions.label: Authority and Purpose (PT-2)
family_questions.description: Legal authority and lawful purpose for PII processing.

questions.label: Legal authority for PII processing
questions.help: Statute / regulation / executive order authorizing PII processing (e.g., '5 U.S.C. § 301 housekeeping authority + agency-specific statute X'). Reference Privacy Act § (e)(3)(A).

questions.label: Purpose-limitation enforcement (PT-2(1))
questions.help: Per PT-2(1) — how the system enforces use only for authorized purposes. Access-control mapping, query restrictions, masking for non-authorized roles.

questions.label: External-disclosure basis (PT-2(2))
questions.help: Per PT-2(2) — basis on which PII is disclosed externally (statute, routine use under SORN, individual consent, court order).

questions.label: PII categories collected
options: Sensitive personal characteristics (race, religion, sexual orientation)

questions.label: Minimization practices (PT-3(2))
options: Collect only data required for authorized purpose
Periodic data-element review for continued necessity
Test / training environments use synthesized data (SI-12(2))
Quick-purge of data once retention expires (SI-12)

questions.label: PII data-element inventory location
questions.help: Where the data-element-level inventory of PII processed by the system lives. Reference RA-8.

questions.label: Consent basis
options: Explicit / opt-in consent obtained at collection
Implied consent based on system context (e.g., job-application submission)
Consent not applicable (involuntary processing under law)

questions.label: Consent-revocation mechanism (PT-4(1))
questions.help: Per PT-4(1) — how individuals revoke consent and consequences (some processing may continue under independent legal authority; some must stop).

questions.label: Consent-record management (PT-4(2))
questions.help: Per PT-4(2) — how consent records are managed (timestamp, method, scope, retention).

questions.label: Privacy-notice content elements
options: Whether disclosure is mandatory or voluntary
Effects of failing to provide information
How to exercise individual rights (access / amendment)

questions.label: Notice delivery modalities
options: Privacy policy page on agency website
Just-in-time notice for specific data uses

questions.label: Notice review cadence (PT-5 ODV)
questions.help: How often the privacy notice is reviewed for currency. PT-5 ODV. Common: 'Annually + on substantive change to processing'.

questions.label: Just-in-time notices (PT-5(1))
questions.help: Per PT-5(1) — when JIT notices are presented (e.g., when collecting data for a new purpose, when broadening dissemination).

questions.label: Privacy Act statements (PT-5(2))
questions.help: Per PT-5(2) and Privacy Act § (e)(3) — Privacy Act statement provided when collecting from individuals.

questions.label: Privacy Act applicability
options: System of Records under Privacy Act (SORN required)
Records about individuals but not retrieved by personal identifier (no SORN required)
Privacy Act not applicable (not covered system)

questions.label: SORN publication status
questions.help: If SORN required: when last published in Federal Register, citation, current applicability.

questions.label: Routine uses defined
questions.help: List of routine uses authorized in the SORN. Reference Privacy Act § (a)(7).

questions.label: Routine-use inventory location (PT-6(1))
questions.help: Per PT-6(1) — where routine-use inventory is maintained for SORN currency.

questions.label: Privacy Act records practices (PT-6(2))
questions.help: Per PT-6(2) — practices for maintaining records of disclosures and accountings.

questions.label: Systems-of-records inventory
questions.help: If multiple SORNs apply, where the inventory is tracked.

glossary.definition: Attribute-Based Access Control — access decisions made on attributes of subject, resource, and context. Common implementation of PT-2 / PT-3 purpose-limitation enforcement.
Removing or altering data such that an individual can no longer be identified, even with additional information. Stronger than pseudonymization; reduces PT applicability.
Per Privacy Act § (a)(8), formal agreement governing computerized comparisons of records about individuals. Subject to PT-8 controls.
Per PT-4, voluntary agreement to processing of one's PII. May be explicit (opt-in), implied, or statutorily authorized.
Federal-agency body responsible for oversight of computer-matching agreements. Per Privacy Act § (u).
Fair Information Practice Principles — foundational principles for PII handling: notice, choice, access, accuracy, security, accountability.
Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act — federal law protecting genetic information.
Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act — federal privacy law for Protected Health Information (PHI).
Privacy-notice approach providing a short summary at point of collection plus a detailed link. Best practice per NIST IR 8062.
Per PT-3(2), collection / processing of only the PII data elements necessary for the authorized purpose.
OMB Memorandum M-03-22 — guidance for implementing the Privacy Provisions of the E-Government Act of 2002, including PIA requirements.
OMB Memorandum M-17-12 — Preparing for and Responding to a Breach of Personally Identifiable Information. Drives PT incident-notification timelines.
OMB Memorandum M-07-16 — Safeguarding Against and Responding to the Breach of Personally Identifiable Information. Emphasizes SSN reduction.
Privacy Impact Assessment — analysis of how PII is collected, used, shared, maintained, and disposed of. Per RA-8 / E-Government Act § 208.
Protected Health Information — health data subject to HIPAA. Special category under PT-7.
Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. § 552a) — federal law governing collection, maintenance, use, and dissemination of PII held by federal agencies.
Replacing direct identifiers with consistent pseudonyms, allowing record-linkage without revealing identity. Re-identifiable; PT controls still apply.
Per Privacy Act § (a)(7), a use of records consistent with the purpose for which the records were collected. Routine uses are published in the SORN.
Senior Agency Official for Privacy — federal-agency role accountable for the privacy program. Common PT-2 governance role.
System of Records Notice — Privacy Act § (e)(4) notice published in the Federal Register describing a system of records, its categories, routine uses, etc. Per PT-6.
Social Security Number — sensitive PII subject to PT-7(1) reduction practices.
Per Privacy Act § (a)(5), a group of records under control of an agency from which information is retrieved by personal identifier.
